name: pdk-leeghwater-pipeline
instr:
Our shop's job is moving to one load per day: each task runs `python -m shop run <pipeline> --start <day> --end <next day>`, and a backfill runs the same over past days. leeghwater has no such window yet.

With `--start` and `--end`, every incremental resource of the pipeline should load only the rows whose cursor is at or after `--start` and before `--end`. Cursors compare as instants. A date, in the options or in the data, means midnight UTC, and a time without an offset is UTC. A row with no cursor value is in no window. A window run must leave the incremental state alone: it loads its whole window whatever ran before, and the next run without a window carries on as if the window run never happened. Running the days one by one must give the same tables as one run over the whole range, and running a window again changes nothing.

A window run of a pipeline with a resource that has no incremental cursor fails with exit 1 before anything loads, and names that resource. So does a window with only one end, or with `--end` not after `--start`. The run's first lines and `doctor` show the window.

It has to work on our real exports: the project and a week of them are in /data/shop (`cd /data/shop && python -m shop list`). The rules in /app/CLAUDE.md and /app/CONTRIBUTING.md apply. There's no network; dlt and DuckDB are installed.
